results.title: Authentication
excerpts:
# Authentication

> Choose between API keys, hosted MCP and OAuth for calling Firecrawl

There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.

## Which should I use?

| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | [API key](#api-key) | `api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in [API keys](firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys). |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | [Hosted MCP with an API key](#hosted-mcp-with-an-api-key) | `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | [MCP OAuth](#mcp-oauth) | `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under [Connected apps in Settings](firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=mcp). |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | [OAuth for apps](#oauth-for-apps) | `api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use [Firecrawl for Platforms](docs.firecrawl.dev/firecrawl-for-platforms.md) instead.

A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See [No API key (keyless)](#no-api-key-keyless).

## API key

Create a key in the [dashboard](firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys) and send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY`. The SDKs take it as `apiKey`. A key has full access to the team that owns it, so keep it on your server. See [Key restrictions](docs.firecrawl.dev/features/key-restrictions.md) to limit what a key can do.

## Hosted MCP with an API key

Point your MCP client at `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` and add the API key as a bearer token in the client config. Setup for each client is in [Add an API key](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/keyless.md#add-an-api-key).

## MCP OAuth

Point your MCP client at `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`. The client opens a browser, the user signs in and picks a team, and Firecrawl creates a dedicated key for that connection. The client never sees the key. The native ChatGPT and Claude connectors use this flow automatically. Tokens from this flow work only on the MCP server, not on the REST API. See [MCP sign-in](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/oauth.md).

## OAuth for apps

Send the user through Firecrawl's OAuth flow with `resource=api.firecrawl.dev/`. Your app gets an `fco_` access token that works on the REST API in place of an API key, plus an `fcr_` refresh token.

* Each connection gets its own key. Your app never sees it, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn't affect the connection.
* The connection is listed under [Connected apps in Settings](firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=mcp), where the user can revoke it.
* Refresh tokens rotate and work once. Reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole connection.

The full flow is in [OAuth for apps](docs.firecrawl.dev/oauth.md).

## No API key (keyless)

These REST endpoints work without an API key:

* `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse` (including `/v2/parse/upload-url`)
* `/v2/scrape/{jobId}/interact`
* `/v1/scrape` and `/v1/search`
* On Firecrawl Cloud, the research, developer and government search endpoints

Every other endpoint, including crawl, map, extract, agent, batch scrape and job status, needs a key. Calling one without a key returns `401`.

To make a keyless request, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely. A header with an empty token, such as `Authorization: Bearer` with nothing after it, is rejected with `401 Unauthorized: Token missing`.

...

Keyless usage is free and limited per IP address. The limits vary with demand, and a `429` response means you've reached them. [Sign up for a free API key](firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys) to use every endpoint with higher limits. See [Keyless (no API key)](docs.firecrawl.dev/rate-limits.md#keyless-no-api-key) on the rate limits page.

results.title: Firecrawl MCP: Get Started
excerpts:
Connect Firecrawl MCP

Choose account OAuth, unattended API-key, or keyless Firecrawl MCP setup.
Use the hosted Firecrawl MCP service in one of three modes. Choose based on whether a person can sign in and whether the client can securely store an API key.

Connect an account

Use this mode for an interactive, OAuth-capable client such as Claude or Codex. Add this URL to the client; it discovers Firecrawl's authorization metadata, opens the browser, and asks you to approve the team it should use.
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth
The client receives short-lived, resource-bound tokens rather than your Firecrawl API key. You can review and revoke access from MCP settings.
If the client asks for an OAuth Client ID or Client Secret, leave both blank. Compatible clients use Client ID Metadata Documents or Dynamic Client Registration.

Run unattended

Use this mode for CI, servers, scripts, or any runtime without a browser. Keep the API key in an environment variable or secret store and send it as an Authorization header.
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>
This uses the full Firecrawl MCP tool surface. New configurations should not put an API key in the URL or commit it to a project configuration file.

Try keyless

Use this mode to try Firecrawl without an account or API key:
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
Keyless MCP is rate-limited per IP and exposes exactly Search, Scrape, and Parse while eligible. Connect an account or use an API key when you need the complete tool surface or higher limits.

When you reach the free limit

The keyless allowance is a rolling, per-network limit. The MCP error includes the current retry time when it is available; wait for that interval to keep using Search, Scrape, and Parse without an account.
To continue immediately, choose one of these paths:
* Interactive OAuth: connect the account endpoint, mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth. For Claude Code:
claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth
Then run /mcp and authenticate in the browser.
* Unattended API key: create a key in the Firecrawl dashboard and configure Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>.

Pick the right mode

* Mode | Endpoint | Available tools | Best for | Credentials
* Account | /v2/mcp-oauth | Full MCP tool surface, subject to plan and feature availability | Interactive clients that can complete browser OAuth | OAuth tokens managed by the client
* Unattended | /v2/mcp | Full MCP tool surface, subject to plan and feature availability | CI, servers, and scripts | Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>
* Keyless | /v2/mcp | Search, Scrape, and Parse only | A limited trial | None
See Tools and operations for the current tool inventory and local/self-hosted availability notes.

Client-specific help

See client setup for configuration examples. If your client cannot complete a remote OAuth flow, use the unattended header-based configuration or keyless mode instead. If it cannot send custom headers either, see the legacy fallback below.

Legacy API-key URL support

This legacy form exists only for existing configurations and clients that cannot complete OAuth or send a custom Authorization header. It is not the recommended setup for new integrations.
mcp.firecrawl.dev/<FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>/v2/mcp
The API key is part of the URL, so treat the complete URL like a password. Prefer account OAuth or an environment-backed Authorization: Bearer header whenever the client supports either. If this URL is exposed, rotate the API key. Never paste it into chat, screenshots, issues, or shared configuration.
This fallback applies only to the full /v2/mcp surface. It does not work for the OAuth-only search resource.

Compatibility during migration

Existing /v2/mcp OAuth connections remain supported during the migration to the dedicated account endpoint. New interactive account connections should use /v2/mcp-oauth; new tokens for that account resource are not accepted by /v2/mcp.

excerpts:
# Get Started

> Set up Firecrawl MCP with keyless access, account sign-in, or an API key.

Choose how the connection will authenticate. Signing in and adding an API key are two paths to the same access: both reach the full tool surface on your team's plan.

> [card] [Try Instantly](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/keyless.md#try-keyless)
>
> No account or key. Search, Scrape, and Parse within daily limits.

> [card] [Sign in](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/oauth.md)
>
> Browser sign-in from Codex, Claude Code, or your favorite harness.

> [card] [Use an API key](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/keyless.md#add-an-api-key)
>
> Configure an API key in your client, no browser needed.

...

## Sign in

Point your client at the OAuth server URL. Your client opens a browser window where you sign in to Firecrawl and approve a team:

```json theme={null}
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth"
    }
  }
}
```

No API key or headers are needed. Review and revoke connections from [MCP settings](firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=mcp).

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is a server URL for your MCP client, not a page to open directly in a browser. API-key connections use `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` with a bearer token instead; see [Add an API key](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/keyless.md#add-an-api-key).

## Client setup

> [card] [For Agents](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/keyless.md)
>
> Start keyless or use an API key.

> [card] [For Humans](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/oauth.md)
>
> Sign in via browser.

Using GitHub Copilot? Follow the [Copilot CLI and VS Code guide](docs.firecrawl.dev/quickstarts/github-copilot.md).

Next: [choose a tool](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/tools) or [run the server locally](docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server/local).

results.title: OAuth for apps
excerpts:
# OAuth for apps

> Let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app with OAuth instead of pasting an API key

Firecrawl runs an OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Your app sends the user to Firecrawl, the user signs in and picks a team, and your app gets an access token it can use on the Firecrawl REST API in place of an API key. Usage is billed to the team the user picked.

Each connection gets its own API key, created by Firecrawl and never shown to your app. The user can see and revoke the connection under Connected apps in Settings, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn't affect it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use [Firecrawl for Platforms](docs.firecrawl.dev/firecrawl-for-platforms.md) instead. OAuth is for users who bring their own Firecrawl account. To compare OAuth with API keys and MCP sign-in, see [Authentication](docs.firecrawl.dev/authentication.md).

## Overview

| | |
| - | - |
| Discovery | `firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization endpoint | `firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation endpoint | `firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Registration endpoint | `firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register` |
| Resource (audience) | `api.firecrawl.dev/` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | Required, `S256` only |
| Client authentication | `none` (public clients, no client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour, prefix `fco_` |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days, prefix `fcr_`, single use |

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| - | - |
| `firecrawl:global` | Full access to the Firecrawl REST API on the chosen team, using that team's credits. This is the default when `scope` is omitted. |
| `offline_access` | Tells the user on the consent screen that your app stays connected until they revoke it. Requires `firecrawl:global`. |

A token can do anything an API key on that team can do. Request only what you need and keep tokens on your server.

## Register your app

Your app needs a `client_id`. There are two ways to get one, and neither needs approval from Firecrawl.

> [tab] Dynamic Client Registration
>
> Register once with [RFC 7591](rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591) and store the `client_id` it returns.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -X POST firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "client_name": "Acme Builder",
>     "redirect_uris": ["acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
>     "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
>     "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
>   }'
> ```
>
> The `client_name` is what users see on the consent screen.

...

## Authorize

Generate a PKCE `code_verifier` and its S256 `code_challenge`, then send the user's browser to the authorization endpoint.

```text theme={null}
firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.example%2Foauth%2Ffirecrawl%2Fcallback
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &scope=firecrawl%3Aglobal%20offline_access
  &resource=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.firecrawl.dev%2F
  &state=RANDOM_STATE
```

...

## Exchange the code

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d redirect_uri=acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback \
  -d resource=api.firecrawl.dev/
```

...

## Call the API

Send the access token as a bearer token, exactly like an API key.

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fco_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "example.com"}'
```

The SDKs accept the token wherever they take an API key, for example `new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fco_..." })`.

## Authentication

The API takes an API key as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY`. The hosted MCP server also takes OAuth. Agents on platforms that support WorkOS ID-JAG can register and get a key without a human signup, and any agent can provision one through Stripe Projects.

- [API keys](firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys)
- [Agent registration](firecrawl.dev/auth.md)
- [Stripe Projects (Markdown)](docs.firecrawl.dev/integrations/stripe-projects.md)
- [Stripe Projects (HTML)](docs.firecrawl.dev/integrations/stripe-projects)

## API Reference

Look up the parameters and response schema for every endpoint, as Markdown. Every request goes to `api.firecrawl.dev/v2` with the API key as a Bearer token.

- [Search (Markdown)](docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/search.md)
- [Search (HTML)](docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/search)

## Installation

### Hosted MCP (keyless free tier)

Connect to the remote hosted server with no setup:

```
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```

On the keyless free tier, `scrape` , `search` , and `parse` work without an API key (rate-limited). Other tools such as `crawl` , `map` , and `agent` still need a key.

Prefer OAuth or an API key whenever the human can sign up. It unlocks the full tool set and higher limits.

results.title: Connect MCP Clients with OAuth - Firecrawl Docs
excerpts:
Connect an MCP Client to Your Account

Connect an interactive MCP client to your Firecrawl account
Use Firecrawl's account endpoint when a person is present to sign in and approve access. The client receives short-lived, resource-bound tokens instead of your raw Firecrawl API key.
For the complete choice between account OAuth, unattended API-key access, and keyless access, see Getting started with MCP.

Connect an interactive client

Point a compatible interactive client at:
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth
If the client asks for an OAuth Client ID or Client Secret, leave both blank. Compatible clients identify themselves with Client ID Metadata Documents or Dynamic Client Registration.
The client opens Firecrawl in your browser. Sign in, choose the team the connector should use, review the consent request, and approve access. Requests are billed to the selected team.
Use the client-specific guides for ChatGPT and Claude, because their setup screens and workspace rules differ.

Cursor and VS Code redirect support

Use the account endpoint only when the installed client version can complete a remote OAuth flow. Firecrawl accepts HTTPS redirect URIs and loopback redirect URIs using localhost, 127.0.0.1, or http://[::1]. For native HTTP loopback clients, the port may vary per run, but the registered host and path must match the requested redirect URI.
If Cursor or VS Code cannot complete remote OAuth in the version you use, configure mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp with an Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY> header instead. Keep the key in the client's environment or secure-secret store; never put it in the URL.

Choose the hosted mode

* Endpoint | Use it for | Authentication and tool surface
* mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp | A keyless trial or an unattended process | With no credential, it exposes only Search, Scrape, and Parse while eligible and rate-limited. With Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>, it exposes the full tool surface.
* mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth | An interactive, browser-based account connection | It opens OAuth and exposes the full tool surface after authorization. API keys are also accepted as a compatibility path.
For CI, servers, scripts, and other unattended clients, use mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp with an environment-variable-backed Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY> header. Do not put an API key in a URL or project configuration file.

Manage a connection

To disconnect a client, open MCP in Firecrawl Settings and revoke the connection. Revocation makes its access and refresh tokens unusable; reconnect from the client to authorize again.

Compatibility during migration

* Existing OAuth tokens explicitly bound to /v2/mcp continue working on /v2/mcp.
* During the migration window, a compatible existing /v2/mcp token can also be accepted by /v2/mcp-oauth.
* A new token issued for /v2/mcp-oauth is not accepted by /v2/mcp.

results.title: Firecrawl MCP tools and operations
excerpts:
Firecrawl MCP tools

Choose a Firecrawl MCP tool and understand its availability and operating behavior.
Firecrawl MCP exposes tools for finding, extracting, interacting with, and monitoring web content. Your MCP client receives the exact input schema for every available tool when it connects.

Tool availability

* Connection mode | Available tools
* Hosted OAuth | Full tool surface, subject to plan and team policy
* Hosted API key | Full tool surface, subject to plan and team policy
* Hosted keyless | firecrawl_search, firecrawl_scrape, and firecrawl_parse
* Local with the Firecrawl cloud API | API-backed tools; direct local-file Parse is unavailable
* Local with a self-hosted Firecrawl API | Tools supported by the services enabled in that deployment
Start with Get Started and pick For Agents or For Humans. Some optional tools can be disabled by environment or team policy.

Choose a tool

* Job | Tool | Use it when
* Read one page | firecrawl_scrape | You know the URL and need page content or structured fields.
* Extract structured data | firecrawl_scrape with JSON format | You have the URL and want data matching a prompt or JSON schema.
* Discover site URLs | firecrawl_map | You need to find pages before deciding what to extract.
* Search the web | firecrawl_search | You have a query rather than a known URL.
* Get data from a third-party provider | firecrawl_find_tools, then firecrawl_scrape with alexandria | You need typed records from a provider in the Alexandria catalogue. Authenticated firecrawl_search also returns matching tools in data.tools.
* Parse a file | firecrawl_parse | You need content from a PDF, document, spreadsheet, or HTML file.
* Extract many pages | firecrawl_crawl and firecrawl_check_crawl_status | You need to traverse a site or section. The crawl tool polls the job to a terminal state before returning.
* Run autonomous research | firecrawl_agent and firecrawl_agent_status | The task spans multiple sources and the exact pages are not known.
* Operate a live page | firecrawl_interact and firecrawl_interact_stop | You need clicks, form fills, navigation, or dynamic-page extraction.
* Search scientific literature | firecrawl_research_* | You need to find papers, read passages from inside one, or follow citations. Searches the Research Index of PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, and arXiv paper abstracts.
* Answer a programming question | firecrawl_developer_search | You need primary-source answers from issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated docs.

results.title: Keyless and API key MCP - docs.firecrawl.dev
excerpts:
Documentation Index

...

Keyless and API key MCP

Start on shared free limits in under a minute, or add an API key for stable unattended access.

Try instantly

Keyless server URL (Streamable HTTP, no credential): mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
* Codex: codex mcp add firecrawl --url mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
* Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
* Cursor or any JSON-config client: {"mcpServers": {"firecrawl": {"url": "mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp"}}}
* OpenCode (opencode.json): {"mcp": {"firecrawl": {"type": "remote", "url": "mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp", "enabled": true}}}
ChatGPT and Claude.ai use account sign-in instead: see OAuth.
This is Firecrawl's keyless mode: connect with no account and no API key. Use it for a quick trial, and use an API key when the connection must run reliably without a person present. If you want to sign in through a browser instead — including from ChatGPT or Claude.ai — use OAuth.
Keyless MCP exposes exactly Search, Scrape, and Parse. It has daily request and credit limits shared by users on the same public IP address. Another person or process on the same network can use part of that allowance.
Use keyless access to evaluate the connection, not as an identity or a production credential. For the current allowance, see Keyless rate limits.

Add an API key

Use an API key for CI, backend services, and other unattended connections. Create a Firecrawl API key, then make it available to the MCP client as FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
The human or system operator must configure the key outside the agent conversation. Never paste the key into agent chat, put it in the MCP URL, or commit its value to a project file. An environment variable reference in a config file is safe; the secret value is not.

Codex

Export the key in the environment that starts Codex:
export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR-API-KEY
Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml:
[mcp_servers.firecrawl]
url = "mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"

Claude Code

Export the key before starting Claude Code:
export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR-API-KEY
Add an environment-variable reference to .mcp.json. Do not replace ${FIRECRAWL_API_KEY} with the key itself.
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${FIRECRAWL_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}

Other clients

Point the client at:
mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
Configure this header through the client's environment or secret storage:
Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>
Start a new client session after saving the configuration. Open the MCP status or tool list and confirm that firecrawl is connected.

Verify the connection

results.title: Introduction - Firecrawl Docs
excerpts:
For authentication, include an Authorization header on every request except the keyless endpoints described below. The header should contain Bearer fc-123456789, where fc-123456789 represents your API Key.
Authorization: Bearer fc-123456789
/v1/scrape and /v1/search also work without a key, with limits. To call them keyless, leave the Authorization header out entirely, because a header with an empty token returns 401. See No API key (keyless) for the full list.
To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use OAuth for apps. Authentication compares every option. ​

Response codes

Firecrawl employs conventional HTTP status codes to signify the outcome of your requests.
Typically, 2xx HTTP status codes denote success, 4xx codes represent failures related to the user, and 5xx codes signal infrastructure problems.
* Status | Description
* 200 | Request was successful.
* 400 | Verify the correctness of the parameters.
* 401 | The API key was not provided.

sources.title: OAuth for apps | Firecrawl
sources.trimmed:
Firecrawl runs an OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Your app sends the user to Firecrawl, the user signs in and picks a team, and your app gets an access token it can use on the Firecrawl REST API in place of an API key. Usage is billed to the team the user picked.
Each connection gets its own API key, created by Firecrawl and never shown to your app. The user can see and revoke the connection under Connected apps in Settings, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn’t affect it.

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead. OAuth is for users who bring their own Firecrawl account. To compare OAuth with API keys and MCP sign-in, see Authentication.

## Overview

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Registration endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register` |
| Resource (audience) | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | Required, `S256` only |
| Client authentication | `none` (public clients, no client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour, prefix `fco_` |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days, prefix `fcr_`, single use |

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `firecrawl:global` | Full access to the Firecrawl REST API on the chosen team, using that team’s credits. This is the default when `scope` is omitted. |
| `offline_access` | Tells the user on the consent screen that your app stays connected until they revoke it. Requires `firecrawl:global`. |

A token can do anything an API key on that team can do. Request only what you need and keep tokens on your server.

## Register your app

Your app needs a `client_id`. There are two ways to get one, and neither needs approval from Firecrawl.

* Dynamic Client Registration
* Client ID Metadata Document

Register once with RFC 7591 and store the `client_id` it returns.

```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "client_name": "Acme Builder",
    "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
    "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
  }'
```

The `client_name` is what users see on the consent screen.

Host a JSON metadata document at an HTTPS URL you control and use that URL as your `client_id`. Firecrawl fetches it during authorization, so you can update your name and redirect URIs without registering again. The consent screen shows the document’s host to the user.

```
{
  "client_id": "https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl-client.json",
  "client_name": "Acme Builder",
  "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}
```

Redirect URIs must use HTTPS. `http://localhost` and other loopback addresses are allowed for local development. A redirect URI may not contain a fragment or user info, and the URI you send at authorization must match a registered one exactly.

## Authorize

Generate a PKCE `code_verifier` and its S256 `code_challenge`, then send the user’s browser to the authorization endpoint.

```
https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.example%2Foauth%2Ffirecrawl%2Fcallback
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &scope=firecrawl%3Aglobal%20offline_access
  &resource=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.firecrawl.dev%2F
  &state=RANDOM_STATE
```

| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_type` | Yes | Must be `code`. |

# Authentication

> Choose between API keys, hosted MCP and OAuth for calling Firecrawl

There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.

## Which should I use?

| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | [API key](#api-key) | `api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in [API keys](firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys). |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | [Hosted MCP with an API key](#hosted-mcp-with-an-api-key) | `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | [MCP OAuth](#mcp-oauth) | `mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under [Connected apps in Settings](firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=mcp). |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | [OAuth for apps](#oauth-for-apps) | `api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use [Firecrawl for Platforms](docs.firecrawl.dev/firecrawl-for-platforms.md) instead.

A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See [No API key (keyless)](#no-api-key-keyless).
